newsitem.title: FRANCE: US, France push for Zaire ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: US, France push for Zaire ceasefire.

text.p: U.S. and French envoys lobbied some 20 African countries on Monday to convince them to push for a ceasefire and talks in Zaire at an Organisation of African Unity (OAU) special summit in Lome, French officials said.

"Joint Franco-American approaches are being made today in a number of African countries to draw their attention to the importance we place upon the end of hostilities and the start of negotiations," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.

Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain met leaders and representatives of many countries who attended the funeral in Paris of Jacques Foccart, a former presidential adviser who was long seen as a kingmaker in France's former African colonies.

Togo is hosting on Tuesday a special OAU summit on Zaire's civil war between supporters of veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko and those of his arch-foe Laurent Kabila, the rebel leader who has seized a large part of eastern Zaire.
Mobutu has called for a truce, talks and the creation of a national council to find ways out of the crisis.

Kabila, his popularity rising with each battlefield victory, says talks must come before any truce. He has called for a transitional government to run Zaire for up to a year but says he will not work with anyone who has shared power with Mobutu.
